brainstorm.name: brainstorm
brainstorm.title: Brainstorm
brainstorm.description: Turns a conversation into a goal: the brainstormer captures the idea and files a proposal and a brief against it.
brainstorm.content:
# brainstorm — the S38 capture lane (criterion 2): a conversation's product
# becomes a goal ROW with the two files pinned to it. The model writes the
# files, files the goal, and attaches both documents; the contract (T12)
# refuses the lane ok until the rows exist — files alone are not the
# deliverable. S39 T6 (CR1) makes it rest: after its capture run the loop
# goes idle — the conversation that produced the goal CONTINUES (a message
# starts a turn with the same conversation agent, brainstormer), and a
# person closes the rest with loop.close when the thread is truly over.
id: brainstorm
schemaVersion: 1
version: 1
after: converse
converse: brainstormer
output: [goal, proposal.md, brief.md]
lanes:
  - id: capture
    step:
      kind: model-step
      agent: brainstormer
      produces: [proposal.md, brief.md]
      emits:
        - { type: goal, attach: [proposal.md, brief.md] }
questions: {}

chat.description: A plain conversation with an agent about a component. The run never finishes, so you can keep talking.
chat.content:
# chat — the plain conversation (S39 CR3/CR1): the loop built when a person
# just wants to TALK to a component. One lane, one ordinary model step by the
# general chat agent, and the loop then RESTS (after: converse) — every
# further message starts another turn of the same agent, streamed and
# steerable like any step, until a person closes the rest with loop.close.
# output: [] — a conversation is not a deliverable; the thread is the record.
id: chat
schemaVersion: 1
version: 1
after: converse
converse: chat
output: []
lanes:
  - id: converse
    step:
      kind: model-step
      agent: chat
questions: {}

conversational-map.name: conversational-map
conversational-map.title: Conversational Map
conversational-map.description: Triages a request, investigates and implements it, then offers an inline review and a security pass.
conversational-map.content:
# conversational-map — derived from opencode/skills/conversational-map/SKILL.md (278 lines)
#
# PARTIAL, AND DELIBERATELY SO. Phase 1 is expressible as a blueprint. Phases 2 and 3 ARE NOT,
# and forcing them would misrepresent the protocol rather than express it. See GAP-7 in
# README.md — this file is the evidence for it.
#
# The superseded design guessed this skill was "the likeliest to reveal a field the reference
# lacks." It revealed something larger: a boundary to what a blueprint is for.
---
id: conversational-map
schemaVersion: 1
version: 1

lanes:
  # ---- Phase 1 — Work. This much IS a lane sequence. ------------------------
  - id: triage
    # "User sends goal/request to task-coordinator. Coordinator classifies into Direct mode,
    # identifies which specialists are needed, builds a structured Brief per task, and delegates
    # inline." No artefact — the brief is a handoff field, as in development-map-direct.
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: task-coordinator }

  - id: investigate
    # "If the request is a bug with unclear root cause, coordinator inserts debugger-engineer
    # first … then cites the report path when building each Brief."
    # The skill lists five triggers for this, and its counter-rule is as important: "When the
    # user hypothesis is clear … skip debugger-engineer — it adds latency without value."
    when: { field: flags.root_cause_unclear, op: eq, value: true }
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: debugger-engineer, produces: .projects/features/debug-investigations/ }

  - id: implement
    # "Each specialist receives its Brief, works from it, runs local verification
    # (build/test/lint), and reports back inline."
    # GAP-8: "Independent tasks can run CONCURRENTLY." The engine is deliberately serial —
    # S5 asserts serial execution with entry/exit timestamps precisely because order alone
    # passes against an errgroup. So this lane runs sequentially and the protocol's concurrency
    # is NOT expressed. A real conflict, not a missing field. See README.md.
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: by-tech-tag }
    on_reject: { goto: implement, counter: retries, max: 2, then: escalate }

  - id: offer-review
    # "The coordinator CAN ask code-reviewer to do an inline diff review before pushing. This
    # keeps quality high without requiring a PR."
    step: { kind: gate, question: want-inline-review }

  - id: inline-review
    when: { field: answers.want-inline-review, op: eq, value: yes }
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: code-reviewer }
    on_reject: { goto: implement, counter: review_rounds, max: 2, then: escalate }

  - id: offer-security
    # "When the work touched authentication/authorization, data handling, crypto, secrets, input
    # parsing, or a new external dependency, the coordinator OFFERS a security-engineer scan of
    # the diff before push (THE USER MAY DECLINE) … never forced on a trivial change."
    # An OFFERED step: conditional on asking in the moment, not on a project flag. Expressible
    # only through GAP-3's pattern — a gate, then a `when` on its answer.
    when: { field: flags.touched_sensitive_surface, op: eq, value: true }
    step: { kind: gate, question: want-security-scan }

  - id: security
    when: { field: answers.want-security-scan, op: eq, value: yes }
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: security-engineer }
    # "Blocking findings route back to the specialist first."
    on_reject: { goto: implement, counter: security_rounds, max: 2, then: escalate }

questions:
  want-inline-review:
    prompt: Review the diff before pushing?
    answers: [yes, no]
  want-security-scan:
    prompt: This touched a sensitive surface. Scan the diff before pushing?
    answers: [yes, no]

# ============================================================================
# PHASES 2 AND 3 ARE NOT EXPRESSED, AND CANNOT BE.
# ============================================================================
#
# The skill's own first line about the workflow: "There is no separate Planning phase. The flow
# is ONE CONTINUOUS CONVERSATION."
#
#   Phase 2 — Git:    "WHEN THE USER TRIGGERS a push (e.g., 'push this', 'branch and commit',
#                     'PR'), the coordinator delegates to github-steward"
#   Phase 3 — Review: "WHEN THE USER TRIGGERS a review (e.g. 'review this', 'review my PR
#                     #{N}'), the coordinator delegates to code-reviewer"
#
# A blueprint is an ORDERED SEQUENCE. A gate stops and asks a CLOSED question. Neither expresses
# "sit idle until the user says what happens next, from an open set" — and the skill's own
# end-to-end example shows exactly that:
#
#     User: "Branch and push both."      → Phase 2
#     User: "Review those PRs."          → Phase 3
#
# A gate with answers [push, review, more-work, done] would close the set, and the set is not
# closed: "also add rate limiting to the admin API" is a legitimate next utterance and appears
# in no answer list.
#
# THE HONEST CONCLUSION: Phases 2 and 3 are not a blueprint's shape. They are a CHAT WITH TOOLS,
# which S5's step runtime and S6's suspension already provide, with S12's actions available and
# S10's guard deciding what may run. The human is the orchestrator, and there is no declared
# graph to interpret.
#
# That is not a failure of the format. It is the format's BOUNDARY, found by the one protocol
# that has no planning phase — and it is worth knowing before someone tries to make every
# interaction a lane.

dev-loop.name: dev-loop
dev-loop.title: Developer Loop
dev-loop.description: Investigates, plans, asks for one approval, then builds, verifies and ships each task, running unattended after the approval.
dev-loop.content:
# dev-loop — derived from opencode/skills/dev-loop-protocol/SKILL.md (864 lines)
#
# Driven by 33 agents and all four dev-loops primaries. This is THE protocol in use.
#
# Derived, not invented: every lane below is a row in the skill's phase table, in its
# stated order. S17 T7 authored it to the protocol's own summary — "investigates
# -> plans -> (one approval gate) -> builds task-by-task -> verifies each task ->
# commits, running unattended" — which means exactly ONE routine gate: the
# plan-gate. Everything else that asks is an exception the machinery raises. Where this file adds something the skill does not have, the comment says
# ADDED and why. Where the format could not express something, the comment says GAP and
# names it — see README.md.
---
id: dev-loop
schemaVersion: 1
version: 1
on_abort: git-abort

lanes:
  # ---- intent and research -------------------------------------------------
  - id: clarify
    # "runs FIRST, before discovery … Always runs; asks only genuine intent ambiguities"
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: intent-clarifier, produces: prompt.md }

  - id: discovery
    # "mandatory every loop" — no `when`. Sets the Legal-review flag that gates the next lane.
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: investigator, produces: discovery.md }

  - id: legal
    # "CONDITIONAL (only when discovery's Legal-review flag says needed) … runs BETWEEN
    # discovery and plan so constraints feed the plan"
    when: { field: flags.legal_review, op: eq, value: true }
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: legal-advisor, produces: legal.md }

  # ---- planning and the one approval gate ----------------------------------
  - id: plan
    # "requires discovery.md on disk first; must honor any constraints in a resolved legal.md"
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: project-planner, produces: [plan.md, tasks/] }

  - id: plan-gate
    # The protocol's own summary: "investigates → plans → (one approval gate) → builds
    # task-by-task → verifies each task → commits, running unattended"
    step: { kind: gate, question: approve-plan }
    on_reject:
      goto: plan
      with: { mode: revise }
      counter: plan_rounds
      max: 2
      then: escalate

  # ---- build ---------------------------------------------------------------
  - id: git-feature-start
    # "once, at build start (before any task) — create the loop's feature_branch off its
    # base_branch (both from loop_get; never invent either) + push it"
    # S17 T7 walk (S16 T12's finding as data): one createBranch lane per
    # BRANCH KIND — the feature branch here, the task branch inside the
    # build ladder below. Without `which:` every createBranch silently
    # builds a task branch and no loop can ever grow the feature branch
    # the merge lane merges INTO.
    step: { kind: code-action, action: git.createBranch, params: { which: feature } }

  - id: build
    iterate: tasks
    rework: implement
    on_reject: { counter: retries, max: 2, then: escalate }
    ladder:
      - id: issue
        kind: code-action
        action: forge.openIssue
        sets: issue-open
        when: { field: mode, op: neq, value: poc }

      - id: branch
        # The task branch, created from THIS loop's feature branch
        # (actionArgs derives the base; S16 T12's two-kinds rule — the
        # POC overlay keeps a POC on one branch, so this rung is not
        # for it).
        kind: code-action
        action: git.createBranch
        params: { which: task }
        when: { field: mode, op: neq, value: poc }

      - id: implement
        kind: model-step
        agent: by-tech-tag        # go→golang-engineer, react-ts→react-typescript-engineer, … — ten tags, one table (T10)
        sets: in-progress

      - id: verify
        kind: model-step
        agent: verifier-engineer
        sets: verified            # evidence REQUIRED by the status machine

      - id: security
        kind: model-step
        agent: security-engineer
        sets: secure              # evidence REQUIRED
        produces: security.md
        when: { field: flags.security_scan, op: eq, value: true }
        on_reject: { counter: security_rounds, max: 2, then: escalate }

      - id: commit-local
        # POC only: "commit LOCALLY, return the SHA. No issue, no push, no PR"
        kind: code-action
        action: git.commitAndPush
        when: { field: mode, op: eq, value: poc }

      - id: push
        # T7 walk: the PR's head is the TASK branch, and the forge
        # refuses a head that was never pushed (O8) — a PR against a ref
        # nobody can fetch is the phantom-ref failure. commitAndPush is
        # what creates the remote branch (CreateBranch checks it out
        # locally; the push is this rung's job). Pushing the TASK branch
        # is not the forbidden push: the "no push in the commit phase"
        # rule is about the FEATURE branch, which only the merge moves.
        kind: code-action
        action: git.commitAndPush
        when: { field: mode, op: neq, value: poc }

      - id: pr
        kind: code-action
        action: forge.openPR
        sets: pr-open
        when: { field: mode, op: neq, value: poc }

      - id: review
        kind: model-step
        agent: code-reviewer
        sets: in-review
        when: { field: mode, op: neq, value: poc }
        on_reject: { goto: implement, counter: review_rounds, max: 2, then: escalate }

      - id: merge
        kind: code-action
        action: forge.merge       # merges into feature_branch, then closes the issue
        sets: merged              # evidence REQUIRED — the merge SHA
        when: { field: mode, op: neq, value: poc }

      - id: close-issue
        kind: code-action
        action: forge.closeIssue  # `Closes #n` does not fire on a feature-branch merge
        when: { field: mode, op: neq, value: poc }

  # ---- post-build ----------------------------------------------------------
  - id: qa-specs
    # POC only: "create/amend the human-followable QA test specs … Never executes tests"
    when: { field: mode, op: eq, value: poc }
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: qa-test-spec, produces: docs/test_suites/ }

  - id: qa
    # "hard-gate (build + full repo test suite green), feature-level integration testing …
    # defects → QAT tasks"
    when: { field: flags.integration_surface, op: eq, value: true }
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: qa-engineer }
    on_reject:
      goto: plan
      with: { mode: qa-fix }
      counter: qa_rounds
      max: 2
      then: escalate

  - id: memory
    # "after QA, before git-feature … (Iron Triage; non-gating)"
    # GAP-2 resolved by S8's `advisory`: a reject is recorded and does not route.
    advisory: true
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: memory-steward }

  # ---- terminal: the abort path ---------------------------------------------
  # S17 T7 (the one-gate ruling): the S8-era terminal branch —
  # feature-gate asking merge-now vs leave-open, then git-feature /
  # git-feature-pr / feature-review — is REMOVED. Three findings, recorded
  # not rebuilt (N1/D15):
  #   F1  Four gates on the happy path (this one plus the two open-question
  #       relays) is a wizard, not an unattended loop. The protocol's own
  #       summary names ONE approval gate; the plan-gate above is it.
  #   F2  The branch needed an answers.* value no lane could set except a
  #       gate — the format routes a reject to one target (old GAP-3) and
  #       S8 solved that by ADDING a gate, which is the wizard again.
  #       Deleting the branch is authorship; giving it a mechanism is not
  #       this slice's work.
  #   F3  Merge is still ASKED (S16's L22): forge.merge is irreversible,
  #       so the execution layer asks a person on an attended loop — the
  #       escalation-shaped exception, not a routine step. leave-open is
  #       what the loop already built: the per-task PRs stay open, and an
  #       unattended deny collapses to a block that leaves them there for
  #       the person. Whole-feature review belongs to the task-level
  #       review step (T8's merge gate), not a post-hoc lane.

  - id: git-abort
    # GAP-4 resolved: a gate's abort jumps here, so cleanup cannot be omitted.
    # T10 flipped: the batch forge.closeOpenIssuesAndPRs this lane carried
    # from S8 was NEVER in S16's closed set (D14 — eight plus audit, no
    # ninth) and validation now refuses it, so the lane does what the set
    # actually offers: close the task issue. Closing PRs is not an S16
    # action; an aborted loop's PR waits for the person, which is exactly
    # what the finish lane's leave-open already admits.
    when: { field: flags.aborted, op: eq, value: true }
    step: { kind: code-action, action: forge.closeIssue }

questions:
  # The ONE approval gate. Open questions are NOT routine gates: the
  # clarify/discovery bodies carry the `question` tool, which suspends the
  # STEP when a person is genuinely needed (S11) — escalation-shaped,
  # never a scheduled interrogation. (T7 F1; S8's `${question.*}` answer
  # folding left with the relay lanes.)
  approve-plan:
    prompt: Approve the plan and start building?
    answers: [approve, revise, abort]

# NOT EXPRESSED, deliberately:
#
#   The dispatch ritual, the FINAL REPORT line, the caller guard, memory_append and
#   event_append — all engine work now (S11's RITUAL and BECAME MECHANISM categories).

development-map-direct.name: development-map-direct
development-map-direct.title: Development Map (Direct)
development-map-direct.description: The short path for one change: triage, investigate, brief, implement, review, then commit and open the pull request.
development-map-direct.content:
# development-map, Direct mode — derived from opencode/skills/development-map/SKILL.md
#
# The other half of the same skill, and STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT rather than a trimmed Pipeline.
#
# What makes it different is not fewer steps. It is that Direct mode creates NO ARTEFACTS:
# "No Issue or file is created." No `produces:` anywhere, no issues, no task ladder, and three
# lanes that are optional at the user's discretion rather than by a project flag.
#
# This is the shape that proves L10's claim. `hotfix` at 115 lines is a compressed dev-loop;
# this is a different thing.
---
id: development-map-direct
schemaVersion: 1
version: 1

lanes:
  - id: triage
    # Step 1: "Coordinator classifies the request as Direct."
    # No artefact. The classification is the outcome.
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: task-coordinator }

  - id: investigate
    # Step 2: "If root cause is unclear, coordinator delegates to debugger-engineer first and
    # waits for the report path."
    when: { field: flags.root_cause_unclear, op: eq, value: true }
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: debugger-engineer }

  - id: brief
    # Step 3: "Coordinator builds the Brief … citing any debugger-engineer report."
    # Step 4: "hands the Brief to the specialist inline. No Issue or file is created."
    # The brief is a handoff field, not a file — which is why there is no `produces:`.
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: task-coordinator }

  - id: implement
    # Step 5: "Specialist follows the Brief, runs local verification (build/test/lint), and
    # reports back inline with files changed, verification output summary, and any surprises."
    # Verification is INSIDE the step here, not a separate lane — the specialist runs it.
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: by-tech-tag }
    on_reject: { goto: implement, counter: retries, max: 2, then: escalate }

  - id: review
    # Step 6: "If the user wants a review … Review is inline, no review file."
    when: { field: flags.wants_review, op: eq, value: true }
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: code-reviewer }
    on_reject: { goto: implement, counter: review_rounds, max: 2, then: escalate }

  - id: git
    # Step 7: "If the user wants the change committed or a PR opened … Otherwise the
    # specialist's work stands as local changes."
    when: { field: flags.wants_commit, op: eq, value: true }
    step: { kind: code-action, action: git.commitAndPush }

  - id: pr
    when: { field: flags.wants_pr, op: eq, value: true }
    step: { kind: code-action, action: forge.openPR }

# No questions. Direct mode has NO GATES — which is the point of it, and worth noticing:
# every other blueprint here has at least one. A flow with no human gate is a flow whose
# safety comes entirely from S12's effect classes, since `outward` and `irreversible` still ask.
questions: {}

development-map-pipeline.name: development-map-pipeline
development-map-pipeline.title: Development Map (Pipeline)
development-map-pipeline.description: The full feature pipeline: issue, task breakdown, a branch per task, implementation, review and merge, then feature verification.
development-map-pipeline.content:
# development-map, Pipeline mode — derived from opencode/skills/development-map/SKILL.md (525 lines)
#
# Driven by 32 agents. The second protocol genuinely in use.
#
# ONE SKILL, TWO BLUEPRINTS. development-map declares "Two Invocation Modes" — Pipeline and
# Direct — and they are not conditional variants of one flow. Pipeline creates issues, files
# and PRs; Direct creates NONE of them ("No Issue or file is created"). Expressing both as one
# blueprint would mean a `when` on every lane and a reader who cannot see either shape. So:
# two blueprints. See development-map-direct.yaml and README.md.
---
id: development-map-pipeline
schemaVersion: 1
version: 1

lanes:
  # ---- intake and specification --------------------------------------------
  - id: feature-issue
    # Step 2: "If the request already includes acceptance criteria and definition of done,
    # skip to step 3."
    # GAP-5: the condition is "the request already contains X" — a property of the input, not
    # a manifest field. Expressed as a flag the intake must set. See README.md.
    when: { field: flags.has_acceptance_criteria, op: eq, value: false }
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: product-manager, produces: feature.md }

  - id: task-breakdown
    # Step 3: "creates one Task Issue per task linked as a child to the Feature Issue, with
    # Assigned Specialist set and initial label pending"
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: project-manager, produces: tasks/ }

  - id: feature-branch
    # Step 4: "off main on the remote (empty initial commit, pushed) … This ensures the feature
    # branch exists at the remote before any task branches are created from it."
    step: { kind: code-action, action: git.createBranch }

  # ---- per task, strictly sequential ---------------------------------------
  - id: build
    # Step 5: "Execute tasks one at a time in order (never concurrently)."
    iterate: tasks
    rework: implement
    on_reject: { counter: retries, max: 2, then: escalate }
    ladder:
      - id: issue
        kind: code-action
        action: forge.openIssue
        sets: issue-open

      - id: implement
        # The specialist named in the Task Issue's `Assigned Specialist` field.
        kind: model-step
        agent: by-tech-tag
        sets: in-progress

      - id: pr
        kind: code-action
        action: forge.openPR
        sets: pr-open           # label: ready-for-review

      - id: review
        # Step 6: "reviews systematically against acceptance criteria … adds label approved
        # (if approved) or removes ready-for-review (if changes requested)"
        # Step 7: "Return to step 6 — still for the same task. Loop until approved."
        # ADDED: a cap of 2. The skill's loop is UNBOUNDED; S13's L28 caps task-level rounds,
        # and an uncapped backward edge is an `invalid` diagnostic. A deliberate divergence
        # from the skill, recorded rather than silent.
        kind: model-step
        agent: code-reviewer
        sets: in-review
        on_reject: { goto: implement, counter: review_rounds, max: 2, then: escalate }

      - id: merge
        # Step 8: "merges the task PR into the feature branch, adds label merged … and closes
        # the Task Issue. Only then does the coordinator advance to the next task."
        kind: code-action
        action: forge.merge
        sets: merged

      - id: close-issue
        kind: code-action
        action: forge.closeIssue

  # ---- feature-level ------------------------------------------------------
  - id: feature-verification
    # Step 9: "When every Task Issue for the feature has label merged, task-coordinator asks
    # the user for final verification against the feature's acceptance criteria."
    step: { kind: gate, question: verify-feature }
    on_reject:
      goto: build
      with: { mode: fix }
      counter: feature_rounds
      max: 2
      then: escalate

  - id: choose-base
    # Step 10: "If an unstable branch exists in the repo, steward MUST ask the user whether to
    # target main or unstable. If no unstable branch exists, default to main."
    # A gate whose answers are a CHOICE, not approve/deny — the format's closed answer set
    # handles it. The `when` makes it appear only where the choice exists.
    when: { field: flags.has_unstable_branch, op: eq, value: true }
    step: { kind: gate, question: which-base }

  - id: merge-feature
    # "Steward reports the merge commit back to the user. Then closes the Feature Issue."
    step: { kind: code-action, action: forge.merge }

  - id: close-feature-issue
    step: { kind: code-action, action: forge.closeIssue }

questions:
  verify-feature:
    prompt: Every task is merged. Verify the feature against its acceptance criteria?
    answers: [approve, needs-work, abort]
  which-base:
    prompt: This repository has an unstable branch. Merge the feature into which?
    answers: [main, unstable, abort]

goal-to-brief.name: goal-to-brief
goal-to-brief.title: Goal to Brief
goal-to-brief.description: Starts on an approved goal, has the brief author write the brief, and waits for a person to approve it.
goal-to-brief.content:
# goal-to-brief — the brief lane (criteria 3, 12): it starts ON an approved
# goal (T13 checks the clause before any row exists), the brief-author files
# the brief row and pins its document, and the GATE decides it — a person's
# approve/reject lands on the brief through DecideBrief (claimed-FROM, so a
# replay cannot double-decide), and revise sends the lane around again for
# the next version (a second brief_create, never an edit of the judged one).
id: goal-to-brief
schemaVersion: 1
version: 1
requires: [{ any_of: [{ type: goal, state: approved }] }]
output: [brief, brief.md]
lanes:
  - id: brief
    step:
      kind: model-step
      agent: brief-author
      produces: brief.md
      emits:
        - { type: brief, attach: [brief.md] }
  - id: brief-gate
    step: { kind: gate, question: approve-brief, decides: brief }
    on_reject:
      goto: brief
      with: { mode: revise }
      counter: brief_rounds
      max: 2
      then: escalate
questions:
  approve-brief:
    prompt: Approve this brief and hand it to a planner?
    answers: [approve, revise, abort]

proposal-brief.name: proposal-brief
proposal-brief.title: Proposal and Brief
proposal-brief.description: Drafts a proposal, gets it approved, writes the brief from it, self-checks the brief and asks for approval.
proposal-brief.content:
# proposal-brief — derived from opencode/skills/proposal-brief-protocol/SKILL.md (833 lines)
#
# Driven by brief-author and proposal-author. It is also the protocol that produced every
# document in docs/aeon/ — which makes it the one whose output this repository is made of.
#
# A THIRD STRUCTURAL SHAPE. dev-loop and development-map both END IN A MERGE. This one ends in
# an approved document and a handoff: there is nothing to merge, no iterating lane, and no code
# action anywhere. See README.md.
---
id: proposal-brief
schemaVersion: 1
version: 1

lanes:
  # ---- part 1: the proposal, optional ---------------------------------------
  - id: proposal
    # "Part 1 — The proposal schema": NN — Title / What it is / Why it matters /
    # What exists today / Proposed shape / Risks / notes.
    # Conditional because the brief's §7 is "Overrides to the proposal — Fill, or DELETE IF
    # NONE": a brief may implement a proposal, or stand alone.
    when: { field: flags.has_proposal, op: eq, value: true }
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: proposal-author, produces: proposal.md }

  - id: proposal-gate
    when: { field: flags.has_proposal, op: eq, value: true }
    step: { kind: gate, question: approve-proposal }
    on_reject:
      goto: proposal
      counter: proposal_rounds
      max: 2
      then: escalate

  # ---- part 2: the brief ---------------------------------------------------
  - id: brief
    # The 14-section template. Four sections are "Constant — copy verbatim": §1, §9, §12, §13.
    # GAP-6: `produces:` asserts a path EXISTS. It cannot assert §1 was copied verbatim or that
    # §9's constant rows survived — and the skill is explicit about why that matters: "do not
    # trim them per project — they are short, and each one exists because its absence caused a
    # specific failure." A trimmed brief is the failure mode, and it passes `produces:`.
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: brief-author, produces: brief.md }

  - id: self-check
    # "§13 Pre-dispatch self-check" — six groups, A through F, and A is "Mechanical — paste the
    # command and its output". The author runs it against its OWN finished brief, so this is a
    # step validating the previous step's product, the same relationship `verify` has to a task
    # in dev-loop.
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: brief-author }
    on_reject:
      goto: brief
      counter: selfcheck_rounds
      max: 2
      then: escalate

  - id: brief-gate
    # The human reads the brief. This is the protocol's only unconditional gate, and its terminal
    # one — there is no merge after it.
    step: { kind: gate, question: approve-brief }
    on_reject:
      goto: brief
      with: { mode: revise }
      counter: brief_rounds
      max: 2
      then: escalate

# The protocol's product is an APPROVED BRIEF. What happens next is another protocol's —
# dev-loops-brief runs dev-loop against it — so this blueprint terminates on the gate rather
# than on an action. Nothing is merged, nothing is pushed, and no code action appears anywhere.

questions:
  approve-proposal:
    prompt: Approve the proposal, or send it back?
    answers: [approve, revise, abort]
  approve-brief:
    prompt: Approve the brief and hand it to a planner?
    answers: [approve, revise, abort]

# NOT EXPRESSED, deliberately — these are handler-body content, not lanes:
#
#   The shared discipline (§0 asking is a tool call · §0b show it before you ask about it ·
#   §1 verify before claiming · §2 name the near-miss · §3 numbers and truth tables, never bare
#   negatives · §4 paths). Six rules that shape HOW a document is written, which is exactly
#   S11's DOMAIN category — judgement the model still needs, in the body of brief-author and
#   proposal-author.
#
#   §12 "How to decompose" is instructions IN the brief, to a later planner. It is content this
#   protocol produces, not a step it performs.
#
# AND ONE CONSTRAINT THAT LOOKS LIKE A CONFLICT AND IS NOT:
#
#   "the plan is a numbered sequence, NEVER a dependency graph (R11)"
#
#   S13's L31 topologically sorts a plan's tasks. That is not a contradiction: L31's sort is
#   STABLE, so a plan with no `depends_on` sorts to its declared order and R11 is satisfied for
#   free. Two protocols with different task models, one sorting rule. Recorded because it reads
#   like a conflict on first look.

research-map.name: research-map
research-map.title: Research Map
research-map.description: A planner asks a surveyor for findings and a reporter writes them up: one agent asking another.
research-map.content:
# research-map — S14's demo blueprint: an agent asking another agent.
#
# This is the slice's keystone made walkable (DEMO §4): a planning step, then
# a step that does NOT call a model and does NOT call a tool — it asks
# reddit-agent, whose signed card offers `summarise-sentiment`, for a
# judgement. The step suspends (the process exits; AS4, P2), the task is a
# row, and a completion resumes the loop cold.
#
# What it needs before it can START, not merely fail later:
#   - a signed card for reddit-agent at <store dir>/agentsvc/cards/reddit-agent.json
#     (the walk publishes one; AS2 — no card, no ask, refused at the pin);
#   - a daemon started through cmd/aeon serve, which wires the card store
#     (an unwired daemon refuses the lane at loop start with the honest
#     sentence — never a durable loop guaranteed to block).
#
# The third lane runs AFTER the resume: `report` is an ordinary model step,
# and the loop reaching it is the proof the cold resume moved the ladder.
---
id: research-map
schemaVersion: 1
version: 1

lanes:
  - id: plan
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: project-planner, produces: PLAN.md }

  - id: survey
    # The delegation. `agent` is the CALLER (the planner asks); the skill
    # names the CALLEE and its skill as `agent/skill`. Params ride the task
    # row so a resumed callee answers the ask it was given, not a re-guess.
    step:
      {
        kind: model-step,
        agent: project-planner,
        skill: "reddit-agent/summarise-sentiment",
        params: { query: "aeon" },
        produces: SURVEY.md,
      }

  - id: report
    step: { kind: model-step, agent: golang-engineer, produces: REPORT.md }

tag-only.content:
# tag-only — the bench demo runner's one-lane rehearsal of the tech-tag
# resolver (S13, spec 2026-10-25-bench-demo-runner). Not a workflow: the
# resolver's two honest outcomes both surface from this single lane — an
# unknown tag stops the loop naming the tag and the available tags, a known
# tag dispatches the RESOLVED handler (visible on the step row as the step's
# agent). It needs no credential to show the refusal half, which is why the
# demo runs it live.
id: tag-only
schemaVersion: 1
version: 1
lanes:
  - id: implement
    step: {kind: model-step, agent: by-tech-tag, produces: OUT.md}
